subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: Should package-to-dev conversion permanently refuse every pre-existing `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR` destination—including an empty directory or canonical OpenClaw checkout—and reclaim only a destination with matching updater-owned SQLite and checkout markers?
rationale: This is a deliberate tradeoff between preventing untrusted checkout adoption and preserving a previously accepted upgrade/setup path; source review cannot choose that user-facing compatibility policy without owner intent.

options.title: Approve strict fresh-path conversion
options.body: Keep the fail-closed destination rule, with the documented operator action to move the path or select an unused `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`.

options.title: Design a compatibility migration
options.body: Preserve a supported upgrade path only through an explicit, security-reviewed migration that never builds from an unverified existing checkout.

options.title: Pause this policy change
options.body: Do not merge the broad destination behavior change until the updater owner selects a supported migration and recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Approve strict fresh-path conversion
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-closed destination rule, with the documented operator action to move the path or select an unused `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR’s latest discussion specifically routes the updater compatibility and security-boundary decision to this person.
